figures.finding: Since 10 October 2010 St Maarten is a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; the Kingdom reported that St Maarten enacted the transferred Antillean legislation, so the Netherlands Antilles' Labour Regulations 2000 and Youth Employment Decree, as reported below, are its starting rules (its own later changes not read).

value.follows: AN (Netherlands Antilles legislation transferred to and enacted by St Maarten)

sources.said: St Maarten enacted the transferred Antillean legislation
As a result, since 10 October 2010 the Kingdom has consisted of four rather than three countries of equal status: the Netherlands, Aruba, Curaçao and St Maarten.

figures.finding: The Netherlands Antilles' Labour Regulations 2000 (art. 15) ban child labour for children of fourteen and under (children being those under fifteen), but let children do light work typical of children (delivering newspapers, packing groceries) outside school hours and not before 07:00 or after 19:00; the Youth Employment Decree bars harmful work below sixteen, with written exemptions from the Director of the Labour Affairs Department; young people of 15 to 18 are barred from night and hazardous work.

value.exemption: written application to the Director of the Labour Affairs Department

figures.applies: Sint Maarten, as Antillean law it enacted; the Kingdom's 2006 report on the Antillean rules.

sources.said: Article 15 of the Labour Regulations specifies that this ban applies to children aged 14 and under.
They may not, however, do this kind of work during school hours, or before 07.00 or after 19.00.
Should an employer wish to do so, he must apply in writing to the Director of the Labour Affairs Department.
